note: The career's choice scenes (track-viewer/src/game/career/choices.js, docs/career-mode.md 6.9). A scene arrives in the inbox when its trigger holds (the predicate is in choices.js) and the week's seeded roll is under its chance: one a week at most, perSeason a season. Each option's effects come from a fixed list: trust, rep, xp, heat (on the scene's driver, with a cause), interest (the scene's team, this season), note (a ledger entry), flag (one race), mood (every sponsor's goodwill, within the Sponsor Challenge cap) and story. effectText is what the button says; {who}, {surname}, {team}, {stake} and {gp} are filled from the scene. An unanswered scene takes its default option when the week ends, and the inbox says so. Text is invented; no LLM writes it.

scenes.title: The papers link you with {team}
scenes.body: {who}'s seat at {team} is up for renewal, and your name is on the shortlist. The press want to know if you are talking to them.

options.label: Keep them guessing
options.effectText: Reputation +4, team trust -3, and {team} keener on you this season

stoke.title: {me} will not rule out {team}
stoke.body: Asked about {who}'s seat at {team}, {me} smiled and changed the subject. Their own team did not smile.

scenes.title: {who} calls you out
scenes.body: {who} told the press they will finish ahead of you at the {gp}. The paddock is waiting for your answer.

options.label: Accept the challenge
options.effectText: Finish ahead of {surname} at the {gp}: reputation +{stake} and 60 XP. Finish behind: reputation -4

accept.title: {me} accepts {surname}'s challenge
accept.body: "See you on Sunday," {me} said about {who}. The {gp} has a second race inside it now.

won.title: {me} answers {surname}
won.body: {who} said they would finish ahead. At the {gp} they did not, and {me} made sure everyone noticed.

lost.title: {surname} wins the callout
lost.body: {who} promised to finish ahead of {me} at the {gp}, and did. {me} had nothing to say afterwards.

scenes.title: Press conference after the {gp}
scenes.body: {result} at the {gp}, where the paddock expected P{exp}. The microphones are waiting. How do you play it?

bold.title: {me} takes aim at {surname}
bold.body: After the {gp}, {me} had more to say about {who} than about their own race. {surname} has been told.
